story_plan.thesis: The single Reuters-origin report describes gold and three other precious metals falling, complicating a simple safe-haven shorthand without proving what caused the moves.
story_plan.lead_direction: Anchor the analysis in Reuters October 23 report and its specific spot-gold reading at 15:20 UTC, then use a labelled four-metal comparison to show reported declines. Separate intraday observation from publication, weekly trajectory and any later outcome; no market-close claim.
story_plan.countercase: A common reported direction is not proof of a common cause. Different industrial exposures, liquidity and observation conventions could matter, but this packet measures none of those channels and supplies no independent causal confirmation.
story_plan.watchpoint: Later separately admitted comparable-clock metals, energy and rate-expectation evidence could test the proposed mechanism; absent those inputs, retain attributed framing and uncertainty rather than a forecast or trading inference.

chart_plan.period_binding: 2026-10-23 is the exact document publication date component; the body observation clauses do not repeat the date.
chart_plan.timing_limit: Only spot gold explicitly has a 15:20 UTC reading. The four metals have no proven exact shared observation clock in this packet. Compare reported percentage changes, not synchronized closes or measured correlation.
chart_plan.presentation: One categorical comparison; code parses the explicit negative_evidence to signed declines. Value_text preserves original positive magnitude spelling, with direction retained separately. Do not add the separate 4% weekly gold move to this comparison or invent historical points.
chart_plan.observation_scope: ACTUAL denotes a reported observation in one Reuters-origin report syndicated by Kitco; it grants no independent underlying-event confirmation, new source, probability or causal proof.
chart_plan.source_expression_scope: Independent attributed paraphrase and original deterministic chart only; no copied publisher prose, photograph or chart.
